Regression estimates the conditional mean $g(x)=E(Y\mid X=x)$. The examples
below show local-constant and local-linear estimates of $g(x)$, followed by a
mixed-data bandwidth workflow. They are teaching examples rather than
reproductions of published empirical estimates.

## A first conditional-mean example

This is a streamlined version of
[`regression_intro_a.R`](www/Regression/regression_intro_a.R). The bundled
`cps71` data contain 205 male grade-13 graduates sampled from the 1971 Canadian
Census Public Use Tapes. The data were supplied by Aman Ullah and are documented
in Pagan and Ullah (1999).

```r
## Estimate g(age) with local-constant and local-linear regressions
library(np)
data(cps71, package = "np")

fit_lc <- npreg(logwage ~ age, data = cps71)
fit_ll <- npreg(logwage ~ age, data = cps71, regtype = "ll")

## Plot the first fit, then add the second fit and a legend
plot(fit_lc)
age_order <- order(cps71$age)
lines(cps71$age[age_order], fitted(fit_ll)[age_order],
  col = 2, lty = 2)

legend("topleft",
  c("Local constant", "Local linear"),
  lty = c(1, 2),
  col = c(1, 2),
  bty = "n")
```

## A small bandwidth-selection example

The next block is a Gallery-authored simulation. It isolates the workflow for
mixed continuous and unordered predictors; it is not adapted from an empirical
application.

```r
## Simulate a small mixed-data example and choose the bandwidth explicitly
library(np)

set.seed(42)
n <- 1000
x <- runif(n)
z1 <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
z2 <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
y <- cos(2 * pi * x) + z1 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.25)
z1 <- factor(z1)
z2 <- factor(z2)
mydat <- data.frame(y, x, z1, z2)

## Fit from the saved bandwidth object, then inspect both summaries
bw <- npregbw(y ~ x + z1 + z2, regtype = "ll", bwmethod = "cv.aic", data = mydat)
fit <- npreg(bws = bw, data = mydat)

summary(bw)
summary(fit)
```

- Simple univariate local constant and local linear regression: [regression_intro_a.R](www/Regression/regression_intro_a.R)

## Causal inference examples

[Causal Inference with Local Polynomials](causal_inference.qmd) uses `npreg`
for a sharp regression-discontinuity estimate and a randomized-trial
treatment-effect curve. The standalone scripts reproduce author-package
results, including bias-corrected inference; the trial example adds a
simultaneous band over a fixed evaluation grid.

## Notes

- Use the full scripts when you want more commentary than the short code blocks
  provide.
- Some examples call for additional packages. Where that is the case, the script itself says so.
- The older `npglpreg` route is deprecated. For a functional replacement, use `npreg(..., nomad = "auto")` in `np` or `npRmpi`.
- The `wage1` multivariate example is available under
  [Multivariate Regression and Prediction](multivariate_regression.qmd).
- For plotting objects, gradients, and uncertainty summaries, see [Plotting and Intervals](plotting_and_intervals.qmd).
